a-slice-of-apple-costs-about-1700-slice.text:
- Claim in post: "The Company Law Committee recommended in 2022 that the Companies Act be amended to permit issuance and transfer of fractional shares in dematerialised form — that amendment has not been made." Related lines: "needs a Companies Act amendment that hasn't happened yet". The fix list says: "The Ministry of Corporate Affairs should publish a draft amendment, with a consultation deadline".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The bill exists, without fractional shares.** Per search summaries, a Companies Amendment Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 23 March 2026, before this post (11 Aug 2026), and leaves out any provision for fractional shares. A government source quoted in the coverage says the omission was deliberate: fractional shares without voting rights could weaken protections for minority shareholders.
  - **SEBI's request.** Reports from August 2026 say SEBI has asked the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to add fractional-share issuance and holding to the bill.
  - **No change found.** No report says the bill has passed, that fractional shares were added, or that the Xaults sandbox has graduated. So "has not been made" is still true.
  - **What the post misses.** The live legislative vehicle and the open SEBI–MCA disagreement. The post's ask for a "draft amendment" now points at a bill that is already in Parliament.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.5paisa.com/news/sebi-seeks-legal-recognition-for-fractional-shares-under-companies-amendment-bill
  - https://caalley.com/news-updates/indian-news/sebi-seeks-inclusion-of-fractional-shares-in-companies-amendment-bill
  - https://www.sansalegal.com/post/sebi-seeks-inclusion-of-fractional-shares-in-companies-amendment-bill-2026-what-it-means-for-invest
  - https://ksandk.com/news/surbhi-kapoor-fractional-shares-companies-bill-india/
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The Companies Act change is still not made, but there is now a bill to watch. Press reports say a Companies Amendment Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha on 23 March 2026 left out fractional shares, reportedly over minority-shareholder concerns. In August 2026 SEBI asked the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to add them. We found no report that this has happened."
- Confidence: Several outlets (5paisa, CA Alley, two law-firm notes) agree on SEBI's request and the omission. The 23 March 2026 introduction date comes from one summary and is otherwise unverified. The exact date of the SEBI request within August 2026 is unverified, so it may be after this post.

biomass-power-at-night-dispatchable.text:
- Claim in post: "the country has set a goal of installing 250 million smart meters by 2026". Section 5 repeats it: "gated behind a 250-million-smart-meter rollout target for 2026".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The 2026 target has lapsed.** The RDSS scheme's original sunset date was 31 March 2026. Press summaries report that the Centre extended RDSS by two years, to 31 March 2028, with progress at about 28%. Mercom's summary says the Ministry of Power told a parliamentary standing committee that the scheme needs an extension to FY2028.
  - **Installations.** Business Standard's topic page summary says 5.83 crore smart meters had been installed by 15 February 2026 against the 25 crore target. The Secretariat puts the RDSS portion at 5.73 crore.
  - **Effect on the post.** Its point (the ToD price signal reaches only part of the consumer base) is reinforced, not weakened.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://thesecretariat.in/article/smart-meter-mission-loses-momentum-as-installation-targets-slip
  - https://www.business-standard.com/topic/smart-meter
  - https://mercomindia.com/adani-energy-solutions-delivers-10-million-smart-meters-across-five-discoms
  - https://www.careratings.com/uploads/newsfiles/1743153302_Smart%20Meter%20-%20CareEdge%20Report.pdf
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The 250 million smart-meter goal for 2026 was not met. Press reports put installations at about 5.8 crore by mid-February 2026, and say the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme behind the rollout has been extended to March 2028. That makes the point above stronger: most consumers are still not on Time-of-Day rates."
- Confidence: Business Standard, The Secretariat, Mercom and CareEdge agree in direction. The installed counts differ slightly between sources (5.73 vs 5.83 crore). No official ministry notice of the extension was seen, so the March 2028 date rests on press reports.

- Claim in post: "The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission's proposed RE Tariff Order for the third year of the current Control Period (FY2026-27) sets the normative capital cost for a Rankine-cycle biomass power project at ₹638–744 lakh per MW". The sources line also cites the "proposed RE Tariff Order".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The order is now final.** Per search summaries, CERC issued its final generic tariff order for FY2026-27 on 23 August 2026 (Petition No. 12/SM/2026), three days after this post (20 Aug 2026). The draft was issued 3 July 2026.
  - **Coverage.** The order covers small hydro, Rankine-cycle and gasifier biomass, non-fossil co-generation, biogas and RDF-based MSW projects commissioned from 1 August 2026 to 31 March 2027.
  - **Inputs reported.** CERC reportedly kept the normative capital costs from its 2024 regulations. It set the normative interest rate at 10.71% (average one-year SBI MCLR plus 200 basis points), with 70:30 debt-equity.
  - **Not seen.** The final biomass tariffs per kWh did not appear in the summaries. Whether the post's ₹9.6–11.1/kWh range still holds is unverified.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://teamleaseregtech.com/updates/article/59407/cerc-issued-a-notification-regarding-the-levellised-generic-re-tariff-
  - https://powerpeakdigest.com/cerc-fy27-generic-renewable-tariffs-small-hydro-biomass/
  - https://solarquarter.com/2026/08/24/cerc-initiates-fy-2026-27-generic-tariff-determination-for-renewable-energy-projects/
  - https://solarquarter.com/2026/07/08/cerc-issues-draft-generic-renewable-energy-tariffs-for-projects-commissioning-in-fy-2026-27/
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. CERC finalised its FY2026-27 generic renewable tariff order on 23 August 2026, after this piece was written. Press summaries say it kept the normative capital costs used above. We have not checked the final levellised biomass tariffs against the ₹9.6–11.1/kWh range quoted from the proposed order."
- Confidence: Two trade/regulatory-update sites agree on the 23 August 2026 order date and the retained capital costs. The final tariff figures are unverified. Severity could drop to LOW if the final biomass tariffs match the draft.

ethanol-freed-up-refinery-capacity-for.text:

five-years-and-25000-crore-later-china.text:
- Claim in post: "Against the ₹6,940cr outlay, and the import bill this is meant to displace (US$4.35bn ≈ ₹36,700cr per year), ₹2,192cr of cumulative avoidance since the scheme began is a modest dent so far." The latest snapshot row is "Dec 2025 | 33 products / 48 projects | 4,814 | 2,720 | 2,192". The same section says "38 projects covering 28 products have actually been commissioned". The hero tile repeats ₹2,192 crore of cumulative imports avoided.
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **March 2026 figures match the post.** An All India Radio (newsonair) summary of a Rajya Sabha reply by Health Minister JP Nadda (10 Mar 2026) gives cumulative sales of ₹2,722 crore, exports of ₹528 crore and imports avoided of about ₹2,190 crore. That is consistent with the post's December 2025 row.
  - **There is a newer snapshot to June 2026, from one source.** An IBEF news summary puts cumulative sales at about ₹3,792 crore, of which about ₹560 crore were exports. It says 39 projects covering 28 APIs/KSMs had been commissioned and investment stood at ₹5,210.74 crore across the 48 approved projects.
  - **No June 2026 imports-avoided figure was found.** A follow-up search for one returned nothing.
  - The same summaries say the PLI scheme runs until 2028-29.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.ibef.org/news/production-linked-incentive-schemes-have-strengthened-india-s-pharmaceutical-bulk-drugs-and-medical-devices-manufacturing-ecosystem
  - https://www.newsonair.gov.in/govt-has-taken-major-steps-to-reduce-indias-dependence-on-imported-pharmaceutical-ingredients-union-minister-nadda
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. A later snapshot, reported by IBEF for June 2026, puts cumulative PLI–Bulk Drugs sales at about ₹3,792 crore, with 39 projects commissioned and ₹5,211 crore invested. No updated imports-avoided figure was found. Even if avoidance has grown in proportion to sales, it remains small against an import bill of about ₹36,700 crore a year."
- Confidence: the March 2026 figures (newsonair) agree with the post. The June 2026 figures come from a single secondary source (IBEF) that could not be corroborated, so treat them as unverified until a ministry release or Parliament reply confirms them. The post's argument does not depend on the exact figure.

greenhouse-emissions-reduction-and-cbam.text:
- Claim in post: "what specific CBAM compliance costs Indian exporters in those two sectors will actually face once CBAM's definitive regime takes effect"
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The regime is already in force.** CBAM's definitive period began on 1 January 2026, before this post's 2 August 2026 publication.
  - **The cost dates are later.** The October 2025 Omnibus amendment, Regulation (EU) 2025/2083, moved the start of certificate sales to 1 February 2027. The first annual CBAM declaration, covering 2026 imports, is due 30 September 2027. Certificate prices for 2026 imports are based on quarterly averages of EU ETS auction prices.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://cbamguide.com/learn/is-cbam-delayed/
  - https://cbamguide.com/learn/timeline/
  - https://it.andersen.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Andersen-insight_CBAM.eng_.pdf
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. CBAM's definitive regime has applied since 1 January 2026. Under the EU's October 2025 simplification (Regulation (EU) 2025/2083), the cost falls due later: CBAM certificates go on sale from 1 February 2027, and the first annual declaration, covering 2026 imports, is due by 30 September 2027. The open question is therefore what Indian steel and fertiliser exporters will pay for imports already being made, not when the regime will start."
- Confidence: several compliance-advisory summaries agree. The regulation text itself was not opened.
- Also checked: the India–EU FTA is still unsigned. Summaries report that legal scrubbing finished around August 2026, with signing targeted by end-2026 and entry into force in Q1 2027. That is consistent with the post's "concluded", so there is no flag. The iron and steel GEI targets are still only the 26 June 2026 draft, and no final notification was found, so the post's 27 September note still holds.

india-hit-e20-on-maize-and-rice-not.text:
- Claim in post: "The FCI rice release price. It was revised for ESY 2025-26." This appears under "What to watch". The post also says: "Blending has held at 20 per cent through the current Ethanol Supply Year."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The rice decision for 2026-27 has been made.** The government has earmarked 7.2 million tonnes of FCI rice for ethanol in ESY 2026-27, up from 5.5 million tonnes. A further 5.5 million tonnes of broken rice will go to e-auction at a starting price of ₹2,000 per quintal. Under OMSS(D), the sale price is fixed at ₹2,390 per quintal for November 2026 to June 2027 (NewsBytes summary; announcement date not confirmed).
  - **Delivered volumes now exist for ESY 2025-26.** All India Distillers' Association data (Autocar Professional) put supply at 895 crore litres by end-August 2026, against 1,048 crore litres contracted:
    - maize: 345 crore litres
    - surplus FCI rice: 214 crore litres
    - all grain: 624 crore litres supplied, against a 760 crore litre grain allocation
  - On this reviewer's arithmetic, grain is about 70% of delivered volume, maize about 39% and FCI rice about 24%. That is close to the post's allocation shares, so the post's point survives. Rice's delivered share is slightly above its 22.25% allocation share.
  - No ESY 2026-27 OMC tender volume or maize allocation was found.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/india/india-allocates-72-million-tons-fci-rice-for-ethanol-2026-27/tldr
  - https://www.autocarpro.in/news/india-ethanol-supplies-reach-895-crore-litres-by-august-end-134667
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. For the 2026-27 ethanol supply year the government has reportedly earmarked 7.2 million tonnes of FCI rice for ethanol, up from 5.5 million tonnes, at an OMSS(D) price of ₹2,390 a quintal for November 2026 to June 2027. Delivery data for 2025-26 (AIDA, via Autocar Professional) show 895 crore litres supplied by end-August, about 70% of it grain-based. That is in line with the allocation shares below."
- Confidence: The 2026-27 rice figures come from a single summary; check against the DFPD/FCI order. The AIDA delivery figures come from one trade outlet. The shares are this reviewer's arithmetic.

indias-animal-protein-export-complex.text:
- Claim in post: "$4.06bn" / "Buffalo meat export value, FY2024-25 — 79.40% of total Animal Products exports"
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): Press and secondary sites citing Commerce Ministry data put FY2025-26 buffalo-meat exports at about $5.1 billion, up 25.6% and above $5 billion for the first time. Average unit value rose from $3,236 to $3,591 a tonne. April–June 2026 shipments were nearly $1.5 billion, up 66.6%. The same summaries list FY2025-26's top destinations by share as Saudi Arabia 9.1%, Iran 6.8%, UAE 6.0%, Benin 5.7% and Iraq 5.6%. Vietnam, Egypt and Malaysia, which the post's market table names as leading buyers, do not appear in that top five. The post's roles are qualitative and Vietnam-bound trade may be recorded under other partners, so this is unverified. One of these reports is dated 20 Aug 2026, after the post (5 Aug 2026); exactly when the FY26 figure was first published was not established. The post already uses FY2025-26 MPEDA figures for shrimp, so its headline buffalo-meat figure is a year older than its shrimp figures. Seen: summaries only (APEDA primary release not found).
  - https://www.civilsdaily.com/news/buffalo-meat-exports-surge-25-6-percent-to-5-1-billion-funded-by-a-new-meat-export-development-fund/
  - https://dairynews.today/news/india_s_buffalo_meat_exports_crossed_5_1bn_in_fy2025_26_5503153.html
  - https://indiaseatradenews.com/?p=152829
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Commerce Ministry data reported in the press put India's buffalo-meat exports at about $5.1 billion in FY2025-26, up about 25.6% from the $4.06 billion FY2024-25 figure used below, with Saudi Arabia, Iran and the UAE the largest destinations by share that year."
- Confidence: Several secondary outlets agree on $5.1bn / +25.6%. No primary APEDA or Commerce document was seen. The destination shares come from a single summary.

indias-gas-pipelines-run-at-half.text:

- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): PNGRB's natural-gas pipeline data sheet dated 31 Mar 2026 (20260331_NGPL.pdf) lists about 34,803 km authorised, about 27,905 km operational and about 8,551 km under construction or partly commissioned. A PNGRB statistical booklet dated 30 Sep 2026 puts the operational share at about 80% of the authorised network. No 2026 national gas-pipeline utilisation figure was found, so the post's 50% and 41% figures stand as its latest. Seen: summaries only (pngrb.gov.in is blocked; the PDFs were not opened).
  - https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260331_NGPL.pdf
  - https://www.pngrb.gov.in/pdf/e-publication/20260930_PNGRB_Statistical_Booklet.pdf

PNGRB's data for 31 March 2026, as reported in search summaries, put the operational gas trunk network at about 27,900 km against about 34,800 km authorised, with about 8,550 km under construction. That is longer than the June 2025 figures below. No newer national utilisation figure was found."

indias-oil-psus-say-they-clear-their_012.text:
- Claim in post: "Aggregate, government-wide CPSE compliance runs comfortably above target: 36.06% in FY2023-24 and 43.58% in FY2024-25, per Ministry of MSME year-end figures."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **FY2025-26 aggregate is available.** KNN India reported a July 2026 Lok Sabha reply that cites MSME SAMBANDH data. In FY2025-26, central ministries and CPSEs procured ₹1,15,798.39 crore from MSEs out of ₹2,36,087.44 crore in total, about 49.04%.
  - **Sub-targets were missed.** Women-owned MSEs got about ₹9,059.77 crore (3.84%, above the 3% sub-target). SC/ST-owned MSEs got about ₹3,984.29 crore (1.69%, well below the 4% sub-target).
  - **Partial-year figure:** a DPE monthly summary put CPSEs at 47.21% up to November 2025.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://knnindia.co.in/news/newsdetails/msme/central-ministries-cpses-procure-rs-116-lakh-crore-from-mses-4904-of-total-in-fy26
  - https://dpe.gov.in/sites/default/files/Monthly%20Summary%20for%20the%20month%20of%20August%20in%20Hindi%20and%20English.pdf
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. A July 2026 Lok Sabha reply, as reported by KNN India and citing MSME SAMBANDH, puts FY2025-26 MSE procurement by central ministries and CPSEs at about ₹1.16 lakh crore, or 49% of total procurement. The same figures show SC/ST-owned MSEs at about 1.7%, below the 4% sub-target, which qualifies the 'comfortably above target' reading below. The reply also suggests SAMBANDH data is being used in parliamentary answers, though company-level figures were not checked."
- Confidence: single secondary report of a parliamentary reply; the figures are internally consistent. The SC/ST share uses all central ministries and CPSEs as its base, which may not match this post's CPSE-only SC/ST series. Unverified against the reply text.

indias-trade-story-has-three-big-wins.text:
- Claim in post: "India's exports hit a record US$825.3 billion in FY25 across goods and services combined, per the Economic Survey 2025-26." The opening also says "in the first half of this fiscal year, merchandise exports grew 2.4% while services grew 6.5%".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **Full-year FY2025-26 figures were out months before this post (8 Aug 2026).**
    - Total goods and services exports: a record $863.11bn, up 4.59% from $825.26bn (revised Commerce Ministry data). The April estimate was $860.09bn.
    - Merchandise: $441.78bn, up 0.93%.
    - Services: $421.32bn, up 8.71%.
  - **"This fiscal year" now means FY2026-27.** The H1 figures the post quotes belong to FY2025-26.
  - **The post's point gets stronger.** On full-year data, the goods/services growth gap widened to about 0.9% against 8.7%.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.dtnext.in/news/business/biz-exports-data
  - https://www.etvbharat.com/en/business/goods-services-exports-up-4-dot-59-pc-to-usd-863-dot-11-bn-in-fy26-enn26050603904
  - https://newsonair.gov.in/indias-total-exports-reach-record-863-1-billion-dollars-in-2025-26/
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Full-year figures for 2025-26 have superseded the H1 figures used here. Per Commerce Ministry data as reported, total exports reached a record $863.1bn (+4.6%). Merchandise exports grew just 0.9%, to $441.8bn, while services grew 8.7%, to $421.3bn. The gap this piece describes widened over the full year."
- Confidence: three summaries agree on $863.11bn and the components. The earlier $860.09bn was an April estimate.

mopsws-25000-crore-maritime-development.text:
- Claim in post: "Operational IIF terms (subvention rate, empanelled banks) are not yet public." Earlier the post says "the exact subvention rate and disbursement mechanism are left to the Implementing Agency's SOPs, not fixed in the Guidelines themselves."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **Subvention rate.** A Directorate General of Shipping page on the MDF, seen as a summary, describes the IIF as offering an "interest incentive of up to 3%" to banks and financial institutions on loans to Indian shipyards.
  - **Implementing arrangements.** One report says SMFCL signed MoUs with NaBFID and IIFCL "to serve as the implementation agency for the Interest Incentivisation Fund".
  - **MDF guidelines date.** The same set of results says MDF guidelines were "reportedly issued on February 20, 2026". The post dates the guidelines to the 24 Sep 2025 Cabinet OM. This is unverified and may refer to a different (operational) issuance.
  - **Gaps.** No standalone IIF SOP and no list of empanelled banks was found. The dates of the DG Shipping page and of the MoUs were not established.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://dgma.gov.in/pillar2-maritime-development-fund
  - https://superkalam.com/current-affairs/29-07-2026/shipbuilding-financial-assistance-policy-and-maritime-development-fund-97dd2a4b-2c39-46e9-b6ef-82bcfb9e31df
  - https://www.cavalier.in/cds-ota-current-affairs/2026-08-04/shipbuilding-maritime-development-fund-2026
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. A Directorate General of Shipping page on the Maritime Development Fund now describes the IIF as an interest incentive of up to 3% to lenders on loans to Indian shipyards. Separate reports say SMFCL has signed MoUs with NaBFID and IIFCL for IIF implementation. pngrb-hydrogen-blending-pilots-real.text:

- Confidence: Single source (PNGRB's own brochure, seen only as a summary). The unveiling itself is unverified.

refineries-under-fire-how-two-wars.text:
- Claim in post: "Russia now supplies more than half of India's crude imports"
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): Kpler data reported for September 2026 put Russian crude at about 1.74 million b/d (to 27 Sep) or 1.82 million b/d (full month), against total imports of about 5.25 million b/d. That is roughly one-third, down from about 2.1 million b/d in August, with Iraq and Saudi Arabia filling the gap. Russia remains the largest single supplier. One result headline reported a record 2.8 million b/d in July 2026, so "more than half" may have held around the time of writing. Seen: summaries only.
  - https://knnindia.co.in/news/newsdetails/sectors/exportimports/indias-crude-imports-rise-13-in-september-as-russian-supply-remains-dominant

Russia's share has since fallen: ship-tracking data from Kpler, as reported, put Russian crude at roughly one-third of India's imports in September 2026, down from August. Russia remains India's largest supplier, so the two-zone exposure described here still applies."
- Confidence: Kpler-based summaries agree on roughly one-third for September, though exact volumes differ by cutoff date. The data are preliminary, and the July share was not computed.

sugar-at-5570-kilo-why-cane-acreage.text:
- Claim in post: "Separately, reports suggest India may need to import sugar for the first time in roughly a decade if the current stock trajectory holds." The post also says: "industry estimates put closing stock as of 30 September 2026 at just 3–3.5 million tonnes".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The import decision had already been taken when the post went up (21 Aug 2026).** By a DGFT notification of 20 August 2026, the government allowed duty-free imports of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar under a tariff-rate quota, valid until 31 October 2026. The conditions reported:
    - only companies with in-house refining capacity may import;
    - the refined sugar must be sold in India by 31 October.
  - Coverage (Crisil, Business Today, News on AIR, Rural Voice) describes this as the first such imports for domestic use in about a decade.
  - In late August the industry said around 8 lakh tonnes of the quota had been allocated.
  - **The stock estimate is unchanged in substance.**
    - In late August ISMA projected closing stock at about 35 lakh tonnes at end-September. That is in line with the post's 3–3.5 million tonnes; one Crisil summary gives 3.9 MMT.
    - ISMA and NFCSF put 2025-26 net production at about 279 lakh tonnes after about 30 lakh tonnes was diverted to ethanol. Consumption is estimated at 280–285 lakh tonnes.
  - The existing 12 Oct note covers the price reversal and refers to "stock limits and other supply measures". It does not mention the import decision.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.businesstoday.in/india/story/sugar-price-surge-govt-allows-1-million-tonne-duty-free-imports-ahead-of-festive-season-550462-2026-08-20
  - https://newsonair.gov.in/government-allows-duty-free-imports-of-10-lakh-tonnes-of-raw-sugar-until-31st-october/
  - https://intelligence.crisil.com/en/homepage/what-we-think/all-our-thinking/reports/2026/08/india-opens-sugar-imports-after-a-decade-as-stocks-fall-prices-surge.html
  - https://eng.ruralvoice.in/india-allows-10-lakh-tonnes-of-duty-free-raw-sugar-imports-to-tame-record-prices
  - https://www.businesstoday.in/industry/story/sugar-availability-is-more-than-sufficient-industry-dismisses-shortage-fears-ahead-of-festive-season-552978-2026-09-02
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The import this piece described as a possibility had already been decided. A DGFT notification of 20 August 2026 allowed duty-free imports of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar, by refiners only and valid until 31 October 2026, which press coverage describes as the first such imports for domestic use in about a decade. ISMA's late-August projection of about 35 lakh tonnes of closing stock at end-September is in line with the estimate quoted here."
- Confidence: several independent summaries agree on the 20 Aug date, the 10 lakh tonne quota and the 31 Oct validity. The closing-stock figure varies by source, from 35 lakh tonnes (ISMA) to 3.9 MMT (Crisil summary). The final 2025-26 closing stock was not found. Whether the procurement price for ethanol from cane juice or B-heavy molasses changed for ESY 2026-27 is unverified, since no source on a revision was found. The post's "ethanol prices have stayed static" claim therefore stands, unconfirmed.

the-50-tariff-and-234-one-untangling.text:
- Claim in post: "Investigations initiated 7 August 2025 (International Trade Administration), on $793 million of Indian module exports to the US in 2024; preliminary determination only" (with the AD margin given as "~123% (preliminary)")
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): Commerce issued final affirmative AD and CVD determinations on solar cells from India, Indonesia and Laos around 11–13 Sep 2026, so roughly when the post was published. For India: AD margin 123.04% for all producers, using adverse facts available. The cash-deposit rate after subsidy offset is 107.17%. CVD rate is 126.09%, including for Mundra Solar Energy and Mundra Solar PV. One pv magazine piece gives the combined India figure as up to 234%, which matches the post's headline number. No USITC final injury vote or final orders were found. Seen: summaries only.
  - https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2026/09/11/department-of-commerce-finalizes-trade-duties-on-solar-imports-from-india-indonesia-and-laos/
  - https://www.solarpowerworldonline.com/2026/09/commerce-confirms-dumping-of-solar-cells-from-india-indonesia-and-laos-into-us-market/
  - https://mercomindia.com/us-finalizes-steep-antidumping-countervailing-duties-for-indian-solar-cells
  - https://www.trade.gov/final-affirmative-determinations-antidumping-duty-and-countervailing-duty-investigations-0
- Suggested wording: "Update, October 2026: In mid-September 2026 the US Commerce Department made its solar AD/CVD determinations final. Trade-press reports put the Indian dumping margin at 123.04% and the countervailing rate at 126.09%. A US International Trade Commission injury vote is still needed before final orders issue."
- Confidence: Several trade outlets agree on the rates and timing. The ITC stage is unverified.

the-hydrogen-bill-hiding-inside-indias.text:
- Claim in post: "One set of secondary reports describes IOCL’s near-term Panipat SAF capacity (35,000 tonnes/year, commissioning around December 2025) as running on both used cooking oil and LanzaJet’s alcohol-to-jet technology" and, later, "In practice, the realistic near-term mix is overwhelmingly HEFA (IOCL’s UCO-based Panipat capacity) with ATJ arriving from 2027-28". The sources note repeats "35,000 tonnes/year HEFA-UCO unit reported for around December 2025".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): The December 2025 start date was missed. One search summary cites a June 2026 Argus report, quoting a source close to the matter, saying the Panipat UCO-based SAF unit (35,000 t/yr) was delayed and is now expected to start in the second half of 2026. None of the three searches turned up a report that the unit has produced its first batch or that supplies to Air India have begun. The August 2025 reports say IOC received ISCC CORSIA certification for Panipat and signed an MoU with Air India on 19 August 2025, with no supply start date given; one report says supply would begin "by 2027". Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2723366-india-s-ioc-gets-iscc-certification-for-saf-at-panipat
  - https://biofuelsdigest.com/indian-oil-to-supply-saf-to-air-india/
  - https://ogj.com/refining-processing/refining/optimization/news/55310900/indian-oils-panipat-refinery-cleared-for-saf-commercial-production
  - https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2739936-malaysia-considers-export-duty-for-waste-oil (the only Argus link returned with the delay summary; its headline is about Malaysia, so it is not certain this is the page carrying the Panipat delay item)
- Suggested wording: "Updated 18 October 2026. The December 2025 commissioning date for IOCL's 35,000 tonne-a-year used-cooking-oil SAF unit at Panipat was missed. Trade press (Argus, June 2026, as relayed in search summaries) reported it slipped to the second half of 2026, and we have found no report that production has started. The HEFA-first near-term mix described below therefore still has to be shown in practice."
- Confidence: Several sources agree the December 2025 date slipped, since no 2026 start was reported. The "second half of 2026" new date comes from a single source seen only as a summary, and the link carrying it is uncertain. Whether the unit started between June and October 2026 is unverified. Related point, not flagged: the post calls the 1%/2%/5% SAF targets "indicative, not yet fully locked into a binding schedule". One February 2026 S&P summary calls them "notified", but an April 2026 ministry report still calls them indicative, so this is left as unresolved.

tiffin-meets-thali-10-day-sip-already.text:
- Claim in post: "That specific barrier — the one MRF, Bosch and the rest of this blog's ₹10,000-a-share club represent — is untouched by either product, and remains exactly where the earlier fractional-shares article left it: a real but early-stage regulatory sandbox, not a shipped feature." The post also proposes: "The Ministry of Corporate Affairs should issue a consultation paper on amending the Companies Act’s whole-unit shareholding requirement to allow fractional ownership".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The legal route has moved since publication (11 Aug 2026).** Press and law-firm reports from late August 2026 say SEBI asked the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to recognise the issue and holding of fractional shares in the pending Companies Amendment Bill.
  - **The Bill as introduced left them out.** It was the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, introduced 23 March 2026. A government source cited concerns about minority-shareholder powers, since fractional shares would carry no voting rights.
  - **What comes next (single source):** one law-firm note says the Bill has been referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee. It also says SEBI is expected to issue a consultation paper on an operational framework in Q3 FY2026-27.
  - **Nothing enacted yet.** No enacted provision or official SEBI or MCA document was found, so the post's "not a shipped feature" still holds.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.5paisa.com/news/sebi-seeks-legal-recognition-for-fractional-shares-under-companies-amendment-bill
  - https://caalley.com/news-updates/indian-news/sebi-seeks-inclusion-of-fractional-shares-in-companies-amendment-bill
  - https://www.sansalegal.com/post/sebi-seeks-inclusion-of-fractional-shares-in-companies-amendment-bill-2026-what-it-means-for-invest
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Fractional share ownership is still not available, but the legal route has moved. Press reports from late August 2026 say SEBI has asked the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to add recognition of fractional shares to the pending Companies Amendment Bill, which as introduced in March 2026 left them out. We have not seen an official document confirming the request or any change to the law."
- Confidence: two news summaries and one law-firm note agree that SEBI made the request. The exact date of the request is unverified ("late August" per summaries). The JPC referral and the Q3 consultation-paper timing come from a single law-firm source and are unverified.

uttar-pradeshs-gst-puzzle-growing.text:
- Claim in post: "By April 2026, the first month measured under the new rate structure with a full year of taxpayer adjustment behind it, collection had returned to positive growth, and the registered-taxpayer count had jumped sharply — a pattern much more consistent with a transition effect working itself out than with a sustained economic contraction"
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): Newer monthly data exist. State-wise GST figures released 1 October 2026 put UP's domestic GST for September 2026 at ₹8,882 crore, up 18% from ₹7,516 crore in September 2025. The national gross figure was ₹2.04 lakh crore, up 14.7%. This supports the post's recovery reading, so the point survives with a newer data point. Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy/story/gst-state-wise-collection-september-2026-assam-jumps-88-up-18-tamil-nadu-falls-5-558994-2026-10-01

- Suggested wording: "Updated 18 October 2026. Later data point the same way: Uttar Pradesh's domestic GST collection in September 2026 was ₹8,882 crore, up 18% on September 2025, according to state-wise figures released on 1 October 2026 as reported by Business Today."
